author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Legionella bacteria were found in one of 10 cooling towers at Yankee Stadium as New York City officials investigated a Legionnaires’ disease outbreak in the Bronx, the Associated Press reported Monday. Ten cases and one death had been reported in the outbreak, with three people hospitalized.

Officials were testing to determine whether the bacteria found at the stadium were live. The New York Yankees said no current cases had been linked to the stadium and said the affected tower was cleaned on Sunday. City officials ordered building owners in the affected area to clean and disinfect cooling towers.

Legionnaires’ disease is not spread person to person, according to the report. Culture testing can take up to two weeks, leaving the investigation open while health officials compare samples and continue monitoring new cases in the Bronx.
The investigation will need to distinguish a contaminated tower from any source connected to the reported illnesses, and officials had not said that the stadium caused any of the cases.
dek: New York City officials found Legionella bacteria in one Yankee Stadium cooling tower as they investigated a Bronx outbreak that has sickened 10 people.
headline: Legionella found in Yankee Stadium cooling tower amid Bronx outbreak
